12	This is the posture the `contributes` manifest key already establishes — a pack ships
13	another pack's rules as data (`contributes: { barriers: [...] }`), composed by
14	declaration rather than a code import. The dashboard's descriptor is the same idea for a
15	reader that cannot import anything: `contributes` is read in-process by the engine, in
16	the member's own checkout, where importing `pack.mjs` is ordinary; the dashboard is a
17	browser reading *another repo* over the API, where it is not possible at all.
18	
19	A pack that wants figures on the dashboard carries one file, `packs/<id>/dashboard.json`
20	— the **descriptor** — vendored with the pack like everything else it ships. It declares,
21	in a closed vocabulary the dashboard owns:
22	
23	- the **widgets** it has at all — what each one is, and which **source** its value
24	  comes from,
25	- which of them make the **repo page** card (up to six),
26	- which single one becomes its **mini-card** on each fleet member's row,
27	- and optionally which make a deployment-scope card on the fleet page.
28	
29	The page executes nothing from any pack. Descriptors and values are JSON lifted as text
30	over the API — the same way task-declaration fields already are, and for the same reason:
31	there is no `import` when reading another repo. The fleet view renders repos the viewer
32	merely has read access to; importing their modules would run every member's code in the
33	viewer's browser, with the viewer's token in scope. Data only has to be *tolerated*
34	across pack versions; code would have to be version-matched and sandboxed.
35	
36	## The descriptor
37	
38	```jsonc
39	// packs/<id>/dashboard.json
40	{
41	  "$schema": "../claudinite-dashboard/dashboard-descriptor.schema.json",
42	  "widgets": [
43	    { "id": "last",   "kind": "event",  "label": "last release",         "source": "latest-release" },
44	    { "id": "landed", "kind": "window", "label": "requirements changed", "noun": "reqs" },
45	    { "id": "recent", "kind": "list",   "label": "recently changed" },
46	    { "id": "stars",  "kind": "stat",   "label": "stars", "noun": "stars",
47	      "glyph": "★", "source": "repo-stars" }
48	  ],
49	  "repo": ["last", "landed", "recent"],
50	  "fleet": { "member": "landed" }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	A widget is declared once and the views **select** from that list by id, so the two
55	surfaces cannot drift into describing the same figure differently. There is no
56	templating and no expression language: a widget's `id` is the key its value is looked up
57	under, and everything else is fixed vocabulary. A schema
58	(`dashboard-descriptor.schema.json`, owned by the dashboard pack, pointed at by
59	`$schema`) validates descriptors with ordinary tooling, and a canon check holds every
60	pack's descriptor to it. The page revalidates structurally on read and treats an invalid
61	descriptor as one named fault line on that pack's card — never a broken page, never an
62	invented value.
63	
64	## Sources — where a value comes from
65	
66	Two kinds, and the vocabulary is the dashboard's to extend, one deliberate kind at a
67	time:
68	
69	- **`generated`** (the default): the value is read from the pack's own generated file in
70	  the member's tree, `.claudinite/local/dashboard/<pack>.GENERATED.json`, keyed by widget
71	  `id`:
72	
73	  ```jsonc
74	  { "generatedAt": "2026-08-20T04:12:00Z",
75	    "values": {
76	      "landed": { "value": 5, "previous": 8, "window": "2w" },
77	      "recent": { "items": [ { "text": "REQ-041 checkout retry", "url": "…", "at": "…" } ] } } }
78	  ```
79	
80	  The owning pack's own machinery writes it — a task landing through
81	  `deliver-generated`, on whatever cadence its signal moves. One file per pack: two
82	  independently-adopted packs never share a write target or a format.
83	
84	- **`latest-release`**: the repo's latest GitHub release — tag and published time,
85	  rendered as an `event`.
86	- **`repo-stars`**: the repository's stargazer count, rendered as a `stat`.
87	
88	  Both are platform facts no file in the tree carries and no pack task should have to
89	  mirror. Each comes from a read the page **already makes** for every member — the repo
90	  metadata and the releases listing — ETag-revalidated and shared by every pack that
91	  asks, so a live source costs a contributing pack nothing and the page no extra request.
92	  The vocabulary is the dashboard's to extend, one deliberate source at a time; it is not
93	  open to a pack naming a URL of its own.
94	
95	## Widgets — how a value renders
96	
97	Four kinds, all rendered by the dashboard's own `ui.mjs` renderers, all through
98	`textContent`:
99	
100	| kind | value shape | for |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| `stat` | `{ "value", "unit"? }` | a point-in-time fact — pages in the wiki, requirements in the spec |
103	| `event` | `{ "text", "at", "url"? }` | the last time something happened, and what — "v1.4.2 · 3 days ago" |
104	| `window` | `{ "value", "previous", "window" }` | a count of things that happened, this window against the previous — the writer states the span it counted (`"2w"`), since only it knows |
105	| `list` | `{ "items": [{ "text", "url"?, "at"? }] }` | the few most recent named things — capped at 5 by the renderer, overflow shown as a count, never silently |
106	
107	`window` is the only sanctioned shape for a count of happenings — `stat` is for facts
108	that are true now, and there is deliberately no shape a monotonic cumulative total fits.
109	The schema cannot check meaning, so the descriptor schema's own description states the
110	rule and review enforces it.
111	
112	Rendering is bounded everywhere: labels, texts and item counts truncate at renderer-owned
113	budgets with the overflow named; a `url` must parse as `https:` or renders as plain text.
114	
115	## The two views
116	
117	**Repo page** gets a *What the packs report* region after the core panels: one card per
118	declared pack whose mount carries a descriptor with a `repo` half — the pack's badge and
119	id, then its widgets. A widget whose value is missing renders as the absent state the
120	page already has, naming the file that would carry it.
121	
122	**Fleet page** gets two things:
123	
124	- **Member mini-cards** — a *Packs* column group beside the existing three, holding one
125	  small card per contributing pack. See below; this is the surface with the least room
126	  and the most to prove.
127	- **Deployment cards** (`fleet.deployment`, an id list rendered as a repo card is) —
128	  rendered once, from the packs the deployment repo itself declares; a `generated` source
129	  may name `"repo": "canon"`, which resolves to the configured `canonRepo` (absent that
130	  config, the card is absent and says so). This is how the canon shows recently added
131	  packs on a fleet page.
132	
133	### The fleet mini-card
134	
135	A cell in a fleet grid has room for one short line per pack, and the temptation is to
136	spend it on a label and a number — `reqs 87`, with the rest behind a `+2`. That is a
137	**pointer to data rather than data**: it tells a reader something exists and makes them
138	click to find out whether it matters, which is the opposite of what a fleet page is for.
139	So the rule is *shown or absent*: every mini-card a member has renders in full, and there
140	is no overflow marker, no "+n", no chip that merely names a pack.
141	
142	Four properties follow, and together they are the whole shape:
143	
144	**The phrase stands alone.** A mini-card carries no column header and no pack name — the
145	grid cannot afford either — so what it renders must be a complete statement:
146	`5d ago · v1.33.102 live`, `12 reqs in last 2w`. The pack supplies the parts (`text`,

content.text:
All three landed in the [mockup](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4cfeb34a-b4c1-49a7-b013-8f9dcc68663c) and [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/dashboard-pack-extensibility-ketc4v/docs/dashboard-pack-metrics/DESIGN.md).

**The glyph** is a widget field — one grapheme, ahead of the phrase, so `git-github` declares `"glyph": "★"` and gets ★ 18 stars. It's recognition only: it makes stars findable in a column of numbers, and the phrase has to read without it, so nothing means anything by the glyph alone.

**The typed phrase** turned out to be the payoff for a decision already made. Because a pack supplies *parts* rather than a finished string, the renderer can set them in three registers: the quantity in `--ink` semibold tabular, the noun in `--ink-2`, and the connectives — `ago`, `in last`, `·` — in `--muted`. So `31 issues in last 1w` reads as **31** *issues* in last **1w**, with the two numbers carrying and the grammar receding. A pack handing over a string would have arrived flat and unstyleable; that's now stated as the reason the contract takes values.

**The subrow** is the one I'd underrated. Each member is a `<tbody>` of two rows — standard metrics, then a full-width subrow indented under the name. It's better than "possibly": a column held two cards where a grid width holds six, so the column was what forced the `+2` you rejected two turns ago, and the fourth group was squeezing the three that answer first to buy space for content that differs member to member. Both rows highlight together and the severity edge runs the height of both, so they read as one member; a member with no contributions has no subrow at all.

One correction while rebuilding the rows: last turn I gave *Claudinite* stars and left `atlas-maps` without them, which is backwards — this repo is the one declaring no `git-github`. The mockup now shows Claudinite's subrow carrying its three cards and saying `no ★ — this repo declares no git-github`, which is the dogfood cost made visible on the right row.

```
docs/dashboard-pack-metrics/ — DESIGN.md: glyph field on the widget; the three typographic registers with the composition table; fleet layout rewritten from a fourth column group to a per-member tbody subrow, which also re-derives the bound
```

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". content.content:
Each tile counts members, never things. "47 open items" is not a number anyone acts on; "3 members need you" is — it is the length of this morning's list. A tile is coloured only when it is reporting something, so a coloured tile always means look here.

The last two mornings

The fleet's own morning brief — what the fleet accomplished that day, and the project worth returning to — written by the digest task into the enforcer repo, one file per day. A day with no brief is a normal state: the task had nothing to report, or has not run yet. Both files are content at a path, so a warm load costs nothing to show them.

Fleet activity

[the schema beside this one](dashboard-descriptor.schema.json) and found **by that path**
— nothing registers it, so adding a descriptor is the whole change. It declares the
pack's widgets once, and the two views select from that list by id:

```jsonc
{
  "widgets": [{ "id": "stars", "kind": "stat", "label": "stars", "noun": "stars",
                "glyph": "★", "source": "repo-stars" }],
  "repo": ["stars"],
  "fleet": { "member": "stars" }
}
```

Four kinds — `stat` (a fact true now), `event` (the last time something happened),
`window` (a count, always against the window before it) and `list` (the few most recent
named things). There is deliberately no shape a growing cumulative total fits.

Values come from one of three **sources**. `generated` reads the pack's own
`.claudinite/local/dashboard/<pack>.GENERATED.json`, written by that pack's own task;
`latest-release` and `repo-stars` are platform facts this page already reads for every
member, so a pack using one ships a descriptor and no code at all.

**On the fleet grid a card is a phrase, not a chip.** The page composes it from the
parts the pack supplied — `★ 18 stars`, `5d ago · v1.33.102 live`, `12 reqs in last 2w` —
and sets the quantity, the noun and the connective in three different registers, which
is the reason the contract takes values rather than a finished string. Every card a
member has renders in full: there is no `+n`, and nothing whose only content is that
some pack has something to say. A `list` is the one kind that cannot be a line.

Two things a pack cannot do. It cannot **colour** its own card — colour on that grid is
the engine's severity edge, and a pack that could paint itself red would be claiming
attention it did not earn — and it cannot reach the **ranking**: contributions never
feed attention, member ordering or the rollup tiles.

Costs are the same shape as everything else here: discovery is free (the declaration
and the tree listing are already in hand), the descriptor and values are content at a
sha and therefore free on a warm load, and `latest-release` is the one live request,
withheld before anything the queue depends on.

input.title: engine-pack-lane-shims red on main: a fielded claudinite-lifecycle version imports the deleted engine/remove-tree.mjs
input.body:
`engine-tests/scheduler/engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` fails on `main`:

```
engine/remove-tree.mjs — cannot be imported at all (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND);
a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test
```

The fielded import is `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs`:

```js
import { removeTree } from '../../../../engine/remove-tree.mjs';
```

`engine/remove-tree.mjs` no longer exists in the tree. This is exactly the class the test was written for (#1004): the engine lane and the pack lane deliver on separate cycles, so a member can hold the new engine beside a `claudinite-lifecycle` version that still imports the removed path — and a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test, which makes the converge refuse to land at all.

Not caused by the branch that found it — it reproduces at `main` with no working-tree changes. Whether a shim is still owed depends on whether any member's *vendored* worker still carries that import; the test's own rule is that the module stays importable until none does.

Found while building #1194; filed rather than fixed there, since the fix belongs to the engine/lifecycle lane and not to a dashboard change.

content.text:
Built and pushed to [#1195](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1195).

**The contract.** `packs/<id>/dashboard.json` — found by that path, registered nowhere — declares a pack's widgets once, and the three surfaces select from that list by id. Values come from the pack's own `.claudinite/local/dashboard/<pack>.GENERATED.json`, or from `latest-release` and `repo-stars`. Both live sources come from reads the page already makes; `latest-release` is TTL-cached rather than ETag'd, because `conditional` throws on a 404 and caches nothing, so a fleet of never-released repos would have spent one request each, every load, forever.

**The fleet grid** works as you specified: each member is a `<tbody>` of two rows, so the subrow shares the hover and the severity edge runs the height of both. The phrase composes from parts into three registers — `★ 18 stars`, `5d ago · v1.33.102 live`, `12 reqs in last 2w` — and a render test asserts they land as separate spans with the right classes, which is the thing a finished string could never do. Every card renders in full; no overflow marker.

**Stars moved.** `git-github` contributes it off `repo-stars`, a descriptor and no code, and `starMark` is deleted from the dashboard along with its CSS. A member not declaring `git-github` shows no star count anywhere.

Three things worth flagging. The new `descriptor-usable` check initially scanned `.claudinite/shared/` — it would have blocked members on a canon descriptor they cannot edit; it's now scoped to what a repo can actually fix, with a test pinning that. The consumer-safe-change check then demanded a migration record or a rehearsal fixture for a new blocking rule; the change is additive, so a fixture is the honest answer and there's now a `dashboard-contributor` member fixture proving one converges green. And I ran the see-it-fail pass on seven mutations across the reader, the renderer and the check — all went red, source restored clean each time.

One pre-existing failure I did not cause: `engine-pack-lane-shims` is red on `main` because a fielded `claudinite-lifecycle` version imports the deleted `engine/remove-tree.mjs`. It reproduces at HEAD with none of my work, so I filed [#1228](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1228) rather than widening this PR — the fix belongs to the engine/lifecycle lane. Everything else is green: 2562 of 2563 tests, `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both zero blocking.

```
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ — contributions.mjs (descriptor parsing, source resolution, phrase composition), contrib-view.mjs (mini-card and pack-card renderers), descriptor-usable.mjs (the check), dashboard-descriptor.schema.json; github.mjs gains latestRelease; view-repo/view-fleet/fleet.mjs read and render contributions; ui.mjs loses starMark; index.html gains the two regions and their CSS; pack.mjs bumped to 60822.1
packs/git-github/ — dashboard.json, the first contributor: stars off repo-stars; version bumped
vendoring/rehearsal/ — a dashboard-contributor member fixture, proving a repo with its own contributing local pack converges green under the new blocking check
```

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1195](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1195) awaits your review, and [#1228](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1228) (pre-existing red on `main`) is unowned. The build is proven by tests and the checks, not by a browser — the page itself is only exercised for real once Pages redeploys.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

Fixes #1219. Two tests reddened CI on a change that touched neither.

The rimraf race (ENOTEMPTY on a temp .git) has now been closed three
times — #235, #258, #1219 — and came back twice, because each fix
repaired the one call site that happened to fail while every other site
kept spelling its own bare rmSync. So the retry moves into
engine/remove-tree.mjs, the 127 sites that delete a tree call it, and a
guard test fails when a new site spells the delete by hand. That guard
found 9 sites the git-driven heuristic had missed. engine-tests'
existing cleanup() now delegates, so there is one implementation; the
primary defense stays what #235 built — keeping git's housekeeping in
the foreground — and both comments now say which is which.

The heartbeat tests started a 5ms interval and waited 40ms of real time
for at least two beats: 2 of a possible 8, which a loaded runner
coalescing timers failed. All three now drive mock timers, so the

cannot be described differently on each surface. Values come from the

input.body:
**Closing as invalid — I diagnosed this backwards.**

`engine/remove-tree.mjs` is not a deleted module. It was **created** by #1222, which landed on `main` while the branch that found this was in flight. The branch was based on an older `main`, so its working tree had no such file — while the test reads fielded pack imports from `origin/main`'s history, which by then did reference it. Hence "a fielded pack version imports a module that cannot be imported": the import was current, the tree was stale.

What misled me: I ran the test in a worktree at `origin/main`, saw it pass, and read the difference as environmental rather than as the branch being behind. The passing worktree had the file; my branch did not. The right read of "passes on main, fails on my branch" is always "my branch", never "flaky".

Rebasing onto `05e8867` turns the suite fully green (2586/2586), and takes the `ENOTEMPTY` teardown failure in `canon-packs.test.mjs` with it — that was the very race #1222 fixed.

No action needed. Filed and closed from the work on #1194.
